'''Costas M. Soukoulis''' ({{langx|el|Κώστας Μ. Σούκουλης}}; 15 January 1951 – 14 March 2024) was a Greek physicist, who was a senior scientist in the [[Ames Laboratory]] and a Distinguished Professor of Physics Emeritus at [[Iowa State University]]. He received his B.Sc. from [[University of Athens]] in 1974. He obtained his Ph.D. in Physics from the University of Chicago in 1978, under the supervision of Kathryn Liebermann Levin. From 1978 to 1981 he was at the Physics Department at University of Virginia. He spent three years (1981–1984) at Exxon Research and Engineering Co. and from 1984 was at Iowa State University (ISU) and Ames Laboratory. He was part-time Professor at the Department of Materials Science and Technology of the [[University of Crete]] (2001–2011) and an associated member of IESL-FORTH at [[Heraklion, Crete]], Greece, since 1984. He died on 14 March 2024, at the age of 73.<ref name="ames-obituary">{{cite web |title=Obituary: Dr. Costas Soukoulis |url=https://www.amestrib.com/obituaries/piow0756436 |website=[[Ames Tribune]] |access-date=17 March 2024 |date=15 March 2024}}</ref>

== Research ==
Soukoulis and his collaborators at Ames Lab/ISU in 1990 and 1994, suggested [[photonic crystal]] designs (lattice diamond<ref name=":0">{{cite journal | last1 = Soukoulis | first1 = Costas | year = 1990 | title = Existence of a Photonic Gap in Periodic Dielectric Structures | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume = 65 | issue = 25| pages = 3152–3155 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.65.3152| pmid = 10042794 | url = http://repository.ust.hk/ir/bitstream/1783.1-43967/1/PhysRevLett.65.3152.pdf | bibcode = 1990PhRvL..65.3152H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Chan | first1=C. T | last2=Ho | first2=K. M | last3=Soukoulis | first3=C. M | title=Photonic Band Gaps in Experimentally Realizable Periodic Dielectric Structures | journal=Europhysics Letters | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=16 | issue=6 | date=7 October 1991 | issn=0295-5075 | doi=10.1209/0295-5075/16/6/009 | pages=563–568| bibcode=1991EL.....16..563C | s2cid=250866111 }}</ref> and the woodpile structure,<ref>{{cite journal| doi=10.1016/0038-1098(94)90202-X | volume=89 | issue=5 | title=Photonic band gaps in three dimensions: New layer-by-layer periodic structures | year=1994 | journal=Solid State Communications | pages=413–416 | last1 = Ho | first1 = K.M. | last2 = Chan | first2 = C.T. | last3 = Soukoulis | first3 = C.M. | last4 = Biswas | first4 = R. | last5 = Sigalas | first5 = M.| bibcode=1994SSCom..89..413H }}</ref> respectively), which gave the largest omnidirectional photonic band gaps. Many experimental groups all over the world still use his woodpile structure to fabricate photonic crystals at optical wavelengths, enhance the spontaneous emission and produce nanolasers with low threshold limit. Soukoulis and Wegener demonstrate magnetic responses<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Soukoulis | first1 = Costas | year = 2004 | title = Magnetic Response of Metamaterials at 100 Terahertz | journal = Science | volume = 306 | issue = 5700| pages = 1351–1353 | doi=10.1126/science.1105371| pmid = 15550664 | url = https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000010922 | bibcode = 2004Sci...306.1351L | s2cid = 23557190 | url-access = subscription }}</ref> and [[Negative index metamaterials|negative index of refraction]] at optical frequencies <ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Soukoulis | first1 = Costas | year = 2007 | title = Negative Refractive Index at Optical Wavelengths | journal = Science | volume = 315 | issue = 5808| pages = 47–49 | doi=10.1126/science.1136481| pmid = 17204630 | s2cid = 12535261 | url = https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000010994 | url-access = subscription }}</ref> in [[metamaterials]], which do not exist in natural materials. His other researches includes light and [[Anderson localization]], [[Random Laser|random lasers]], [[graphene]] and [[Surface plasmon|plasmonics]].

== Awards and honours ==
{{more citations needed|date=January 2024}}
*He was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1991),<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=22 January 2024 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> [[Optical Society]] (2003),<ref name="csoptica"/> [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2002),<ref>{{cite news |title=IOWA STATE PROFESSOR ELECTED AAAS FELLOW |url=https://archive.news.iastate.edu/oldreleases/2002/nov/soukoulis.shtml |access-date=22 January 2024 |publisher=Iowa State University News Service |date=14 November 2002}}</ref> and [[National Academy of Inventors]] (2018).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gibson |first1=Kerry |title=Costas Soukoulis elected to National Academy of Inventors |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/665117 |access-date=22 January 2024 |work=EurekAlert! |date=11 December 2018}}</ref>
*He was a recipient of Senior [[Humboldt Research Award]] (2002), and the first Frances M. Craig endowed chair in Physics Department at [[Iowa State University|ISU]] (2007).
*Soukoulis shared ([[John Pendry|Pendry]], [[David R. Smith (physicist)|Smith]], [[Ekmel Özbay|Özbay]] and Wegener) the 2005 [[Descartes Prize]], awarded by the [[European Union]], for contributions to metamaterials.
*Honorary Doctorate from [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel|Vrije University in Brussels]] (2011).
*Soukoulis, Pendry and Smith recipients of the 2013 [[James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials|APS James C. McGroddy Prize]] “for discovery of metamaterials.”
*He was a recipient of the 2014 [[Max Born Award]] given by the [[Optical Society|OSA]].<ref name="csoptica">{{cite news |title=Costas M Soukoulis |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Costas_M_Soukoulis |access-date=22 January 2024 |publisher=Optica}}</ref>
*Soukoulis was selected in 2014, 2015 and 2016  among the Highly Cited Researchers published by [[Thomson-Reuters]].
*The Rolf Landauer Medal of the International ETOPIM Association (2015).
